summary: @servicetitan/anvil2-ext-atlas@4.0.4 ships install-time dropper that downloads Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package's preinstall hook ("preinstall": "node setup.mjs") downloads the Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a tmp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it with a bundled math_init.js as its argument (execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js])). math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-only file (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with hex-mangled identifiers, a large mixed-value string array, and a classic string-array rotator function — its runtime behavior is not observable in source form. The package advertises itself as a React UI component library and has no legitimate need for a second language runtime or an obfuscated payload at install time; executing the payload via an alien runtime also bypasses Node-only scanners. Additionally, package.json declares only `"files": ["dist", "CHANGELOG.md"]`, yet the published tarball ships setup.mjs and math_init.js at the tarball root — the exact two files that implement the dropper chain are outside the author's declared publish set, consistent with a compromised publish path rather than intentional maintainer behavior. The dropper executes automatically on `npm install`, running attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
